ImageDescription.value:
The Massachusetts Institute of Technology's major classroom buildings were opened in 1916. They consist of a series of connected buildings, symmetrical around an open court. This is Building 10, in the center, with the "Great Dome." The dome is 150 ft (45 m) high. It was designed after the Pantheon in Rome. The dome is the symbol of MIT. I took this photo from Memorial Drive in Cambridge.

I do not remember hearing the term "Great Dome" during my time at MIT. Perhaps it is to distinguish it from a smaller dome on Building 7, on Massachusetts Avenue.

ImageDescription.value:
A postcard air view of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology campus in 1975, The MIT Campus is in Cambridge, Massachusetts, across the Charles River from Boston. It is along a wide area in the river called the Charles River Basin. Memorial Drive is parallel to the river.

The original set of classroom buildings from 1913-1916 is at left. Most buildings at MIT are numbered. The Great Dome is on Building 10. The Hayden Library (Building 14) is to the right of the main buildings, and Walker Memorial (Building 50) is the next building. The tower is the Green Building (Building 54). It was built in 1962-1964. It is 295 feet (90 m) high, and is the tallest building in Cambridge.

Kresge Auditorium, designed by Eero Saarinen and built in 1953-1955, is at top left. It is supported at three points. It is Building 46 in the numbering system, but its number is not used. There are dormitories off the photo, fronting on Memorial Drive, including Burton House, my first "home" when I attended MIT.

The East Campus dormitories are at the right. (Dormitories are not in MIT building numbers.) I lived in Senior House, most of which is shown at bottom right.
